text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Liberals face appeals to aid airline: Financial crisis at Canadian creates pressure in the West to help company restructure.
- Defiant Bhutto hits back at foes: Dismissed PM vows to return.
- Clinton begins shaping his second administration: President wants Republican representatives on new cabinet.
- Charity increases still leave shortfall: Canadian government cuts too deep to fill.
- Fidelity fund manager Veronika Hirsch ousted.
- Ontario surgeons to refuse patients: Doctors' group wants job action to begin tomorrow.
- Fidelity ousts fund manager Veronika Hirsch.
- Stocks soar on U.S. election results.
- Ford Canada deal limits outsourcing: Union vows to spread fight.
- Corporate profits '90s' best: Third quarter earnings rise 7 percent in survey.
- Stock markets roar approval of U.S. balance of power: Dow and TSE surge on hope Republican Congress will hem in Clinton.
- Fund manager Veronika Hirsch put on ice by Fidelity.
